env.world: A fixed finite population of \(N=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}s_g\) units is partitioned into \(m\) labeled clusters \(\mathcal G=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) of sizes \(s_g\in\{3,\ldots,b\}\). Potential outcomes are fixed and bounded, \(Y_{gi}(z,a)\in[0,1]\), and depend on the realized assignment only through unit \(i\)'s own treatment \(z\in\{0,1\}\) and its cluster's saturation label \(a\in\mathcal A=\{1,\ldots,K\}\); there is no superpopulation sampling. A randomized design \(D\in\Delta(\mathcal X)\), with arbitrary dependence across clusters and stages, draws the complete feasible assignment \(X=((A_g,S_g))_{g\in\mathcal G}\), where \(|S_g|=r_{s_g,A_g}\) for a prescribed treated-count table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\). The observation map \(\mathcal O(X)=\{(g,i,\mathbf 1\{i\in S_g\},A_g)\}\) reveals \(V=(Y_{gi}(\mathbf 1\{i\in S_g\},A_g))_{g,i}\in[0,1]^N\), and an arbitrary measurable rule \(\delta(X,V)\in[-L,L]\) is scored by the design-based squared error \(\mathcal R(D,\delta;Y)=\mathbb E_D[(\delta(X,V)-\tau(Y))^2]\), where only \(X\) is random, for the person-weighted contrast \(\tau(Y)=N^{-1}\sum_{g}\sum_{i\le s_g}\sum_{z,a}c_{z,a}Y_{gi}(z,a)\) with rational \(c\), \(\sum_{z,a}c_{z,a}=0\), and radius \(L=\tfrac12\sum_{z,a}|c_{z,a}|\). The benchmarks are the unrestricted minimax risk \(R^\star=\inf_{D,\delta}\sup_{Y\in\mathcal M}\mathcal R(D,\delta;Y)\) and its common-probability independent-saturation restriction \(R_{\mathrm{ind}}\).
env.notes: CORRECTED (round 2): this world is LOCAL composite saturation-experiment scaffolding, not a wholesale reuse. `FiniteDesign Ω` (Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/DesignCore.lean:44) is only a probability mass function on a fintype with `E`/`Var`/`map`/`Pr` algebra; it carries no feasible two-stage assignment space, no potential outcomes, no observation map, no estimator, and no design-based experiment, so it is recorded here as SUPPORTING PROBABILITY-LAYER REUSE (a component) rather than as the world itself. env.world: A finite bounded squared-loss decision game obtained by quotienting the experiment by the finite symmetry group \(\Gamma=\prod_{g}\mathfrak S_{s_g}\rtimes\prod_{q}\mathfrak S_{m_q}\) of within-cluster unit permutations and permutations of equal-size clusters. Nature's finite state space is the response-orbit set \(\mathcal K=\{0,1\}^{2KN}/\Gamma\) of size-tagged histograms of cluster response types, carrying rational targets \(\theta_\kappa\in[-L,L]\); the procedure's finite action-index space is the assignment-orbit set \(\mathcal N=\mathcal X/\Gamma\) of label histograms \((n_{q,a})\); data live in the observation-orbit set \(\mathcal W\) of size-tagged histograms of local triples \((a,u,v)\). The experiment is the rational stabilizer-weighted kernel \(H_{\kappa n\omega}\ge0\) with \(\sum_\omega H_{\kappa n\omega}=1\), assembled from the local exact-count kernels \(P_{t,a}(u,v)\). A procedure is a probability vector \((d_n)_{n\in\mathcal N}\) together with clipped decisions \(\delta_{n\omega}\in[-L,L]\), scored by \(\sum_{n,\omega}d_nH_{\kappa n\omega}(\delta_{n\omega}-\theta_\kappa)^2\); equivalently, in perspective variables \(t_{n\omega}=d_n\delta_{n\omega}\), by \(\sum_{n,\omega}H_{\kappa n\omega}(t_{n\omega}-d_n\theta_\kappa)^2/d_n\) with the closed value \(0\) at \(d_n=0\). Its primal value is \(\operatorname{val}(\mathsf P)\); the dual value \(\operatorname{val}(\mathsf Q)\) maximizes \(\min_n b_n(\pi)\) over priors \(\pi\in\Delta(\mathcal K)\), where \(b_n(\pi)\) is the posterior residual obtained by completing the square with the guarded posterior mean \(h_{n\omega}/a_{n\omega}\); rational certificates \(\underline R\le\overline R\) with tolerance \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\), and the compiler \(\mathfrak C\) producing them, live in this game.
env.notes: This is the single highest-leverage reuse decision and it is an exact abstraction match, not an analogy. `FiniteSquaredLoss.Procedure X l u` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/FiniteSquaredLoss/Core.lean:33) is literally a `FiniteDesign R` plus `∀ r, X r → Set.Icc l u` — the pair \((d,\delta)\) with clipping built in — and `risk P tau q theta = ∑ r, q.design.p r * ∑ x, P theta r x * (δ - tau theta)^2` (Core.lean:43) is the orbit risk \(\rho_\kappa\). `Model Theta B X` (PosteriorBarycenter.lean:27) packages exactly \((H,\theta)\) with `P_nonneg`/`P_sum` = the kernel facts (13)/(6); `Model.posteriorMean` (PosteriorBarycenter.lean:79) is the guarded \(h_{n\omega}/a_{n\omega}\) with the paper's zero-likelihood convention already proved total (`predictiveTarget_eq_zero_of_predictiveMass_eq_zero`), `Model.posteriorResidual` is \(b_n(\pi)\), `squaredRisk_eq_posteriorResidual_add` is the paper's completion-of-the-square identity (18)/(38) verbatim, `iInf_squaredRisk_eq_posteriorResidual` is (19), and `sInf_posteriorResidual_le_minimaxValue` is weak duality. `finite_bounded_squared_loss_has_saddle` (Saddle.lean:157) delivers attainment of a design, a clipped decision table, and a least-favorable prior together with \(\operatorname{val}(\mathsf P)=\operatorname{val}(\mathsf Q)=\)`minimaxValue`. The orbit quotient itself reuses `Causalean.Stat.FiniteRaoBlackwell.conditionalMeanAlongMap` + `E_map_conditionalMeanAlongMap_sq_le` + `conditionalMeanAlongMap_mem_Icc` (Stat/FiniteRaoBlackwell/DesignPushforward.lean:122-263): pushing a design along a map and replacing the rule by its conditional mean weakly decreases squared risk and stays clipped, with zero-mass fibers total. Bypass justification for the un-reused parts: the orbit index types \(\mathcal K,\mathcal N,\mathcal W\) and the kernel \(H\) are this paper's exact-count saturation construction and have no library analogue; the sibling accepted-bank module `CausalSmith/Experimentation/EXP_MultiarmSecondorderMinimaxFrontier_Research/Helpers/OrbitLikelihood.lean` (`orbitLik`, `orbitLik_sum_obs`, `labeledObservation_card_ratio_eq_orbitLik`) and `Helpers/FiniteGame.lean` (`finite_orbit_game_has_saddle`) carry the SAME proof pattern in the no-interference multi-arm setting and are the references F3 should adapt; the gap to bridge is the two-stage label-plus-exact-subset local kernel and the equal-size-cluster stabilizer divisor \(\binom{m_q}{(n_{q,a})_a}\), which the sibling does not have. citations.title: On General Minimax Theorems
citations.citation: Sion, Maurice. 1958. ``On General Minimax Theorems.'' Pacific Journal of Mathematics 8(1): 171--176.
citations.verbatim_statement: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be convex, compact spaces, and \(f\) a function on \(M\times N\), quasi-concave-convex and u.s.c.-l.s.c. Then \(\sup\inf f=\inf\sup f\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Maurice Sion, On general minimax theorems, Pacific Journal of Mathematics 8 (1958), Theorem 3.4, publisher PDF.

citations.title: Geometric Algorithms and Combinatorial Optimization
citations.authors: Martin Grötschel, László Lovász, and Alexander Schrijver
citations.citation: Grötschel, Martin, László Lovász, and Alexander Schrijver. 1988. Geometric Algorithms and Combinatorial Optimization. Algorithms and Combinatorics 2. Berlin: Springer-Verlag.
citations.locator: Theorem (4.3.13), pages 113--114, together with Definition (2.1.16), page 53, the oracle-polynomial convention on page 55, and Problem (2.1.22), page 56
citations.verbatim_statement: Output: A vector \(y\in S(K,\varepsilon)\) such that \(f(y)<f(x)+\varepsilon\) for all \(x\in S(K,-\varepsilon)\).

attestation.note: Verified against the primary PDF at the stated locations. Theorem (4.3.13) takes a positive rational accuracy \(\varepsilon\), a centered convex body \((K;n,R,r,a_0)\) given by weak membership, and a globally defined convex function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) whose oracle, for rational \(x\) and positive rational \(\delta\), returns rational \(t\) with \(|f(x)-t|<\delta\). Definition (2.1.16) expands centeredness as rational data with \(B(a_0,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(0,R)\). Problem (2.1.22) specifies that the returned vector is rational, and page 55 makes oracle-polynomial time polynomial in the body's rational encoding and the further inputs, hence logarithmic in inverse binary accuracy. The displayed output sentence is transcribed from Theorem (4.3.13), with notation normalized to LaTeX. One further call to the stated value oracle at the rational output supplies a rational approximate objective value to any requested rational accuracy.

def:endpoint-extension.statement_sketch: noncomputable def endpointExtension (inst) (d : Assignment inst → (RevealedIndex inst → Bool) → ℝ) (x : Assignment inst) (v : RevealedIndex inst → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ e : RevealedIndex inst → Bool, (∏ j, if e j then v j else 1 - v j) * d x e
def:endpoint-extension.notes: Encoding decision: the multilinear/Bernoulli extension is defined ALGEBRAICALLY as the paper's own expanded form, equation (54) of thm:bit-certified-orbit-compiler, i.e. a finite sum over binary vectors on the revealed coordinates weighted by the product of \(v_j\) and \(1-v_j\). This is the right abstraction: it makes \(\overline d\) total on all of \(\mathbb R^N\), keeps the decoder division-free, and avoids importing product-measure machinery for a purely finite identity. Its Bernoulli reading (a conditionally independent Bernoulli draw with means \(V\)) is then a lemma, not the definition, and the quadratic Jensen step (6)-(7) is proved from `E`-algebra over the same finite weights. def:local-kernel.statement_sketch: noncomputable def localExactCountKernel (inst) (q : ℕ) (t : ClusterRespType inst q) (a : Label inst) (u v : ℕ) : ℚ := ((Finset.univ.powersetCard (r q a)).filter (fun S => treatedOnes t a S = u ∧ controlOnes t a S = v)).card / (q.choose (r q a))
def:local-kernel.notes: Rational by construction (a card over a positive `Nat.choose`), with the boundary cases \(r_{q,a}\in\{0,q\}\) total because the denominator is one.
